chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who swore to slaughter his son. He said, 'That is from the steps of Satan.'

key_terms.خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ: steps of Satan (idiomatic for specific acts or movements of Satan)
key_terms.يَنْحَرَ: to slaughter (specifically an animal or person by cutting the throat)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who swears to slaughter his son according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the specific act of slaughtering one's son to fulfill an oath as 'from the steps of Satan,' linking it to the pre-Islamic practice of *ta'abbud* (devotional slaughter) to appease deities. This narration, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the juristic principle that such oaths, while binding, carry a distinct ethical and ritual significance as a form of idolatrous imitation, thereby serving as a practical warning against extreme vows that mimic pagan customs.
